effect: A country facing a security crisis now treats the other side as a threat in its defence planning and reviews its defence when the crisis escalates. The defence planner's threat list held neighbours, declared rivals and enemies at war, each weighted by a hostility of 1 at war or else the rivalry or relations; being the target of a crisis (red lines, a border mobilisation, a blockade) entered only through the small relations hits of those measures, and the defence review was triggered only when the country entered or left a war. Now the other principal of every active crisis, and any supporter on its side that has itself escalated (rung 1 or more), is on the threat list with a hostility of at least its escalation rung / 3 (the game's own rung, 0 to 3, so a full rung-3 crisis counts like a war), and a change in any opponent's rung against the country triggers its defence review, as a war change does (the review signature lists each opponent above rung 0, so a country with no such opponent keeps the game's own signature; after loading a save from an older version only the countries that face an opponent above rung 0 review their defence once). The threat feeds the game's own defence-budget desire and force plan, which close only part of the gap each quarter and stay bound by the budget rules. A partial call-up of reserves before war is not added (reserves are still called only at war). Real-world behaviour: states under coercion raise readiness and defence spending before a war starts (Israel 1967, Ukraine 2021-22, Taiwan under PLA drills; from memory). Day-0 effect: none (no crisis exists at the start, measured on day 0 of seed 12345; AI crises open in the first weeks, two by day 200); starting numbers are unchanged. No new saved state.
